newsitem.title: FINLAND: HARTWALL CEO SEES RISING OVERSEAS SALES.
newsitem.headline: HARTWALL CEO SEES RISING OVERSEAS SALES.

text.p: Finnish beverages maker Oy Hartwall Ab said on Thursday half of its sales would come from overseas operations in 2000, up from 35 percent in 1996.

"Half of Hartwall's turnover and total sales will come from the group's overseas operations, particularly BBH," Hartwall CEO Jussi Lansio told a news conference, referring to Baltic Beverages Holding Ab, owned jointly by Hartwall and Pripps-Ringnes, part of Norwegian food group Orkla .
"BBH's sales are likely to increase two- to threefold in the near future," Lansio added.
Hartwall repeated an earlier statement that Orkla's recent acquisition of 100 percent of Pripps-Ringnes would not have any impact on the businesses of Hartwall or BBH.
Pripps-Ringnes owns one fifth of Hartwall shares and votes.
Earlier, Hartwall said in a statement with its 1996 results that BBH's sales were expected to approach 500 million litres this year compared to about 320 million litres in 1996.
The Hartwall group's total sales volume amounted to 579.3 million litres in 1996, up from 514.5 million in 1995. Net sales rose to 2.00 billion markka from 1.72 billion in 1995.
Hartwall said its five-year agreement on the manufacture, distribution, sales and marketing of Coca-Cola would continue up to March 15, 1997.

"We are currently engaged in intensive negotiations on how the co-operation between Coca-Cola Corporation and Hartwall will be conducted in the future," Lansio said, adding he could make no further comment on those talks.
But he repeated an earlier estimate that sales of Coca-Cola products accounted for about 20 percent of Hartwall's domestic sales and approximately 10 percent of profit.
